queries.question: Where do we read a plain settings file line by line, splitting each row at the first equals sign and skipping empty rows plus ones that begin with a hash?
queries.why: Reads .aions/python.env, partitions each line on '=' and ignores blanks and '#' lines.

queries.question: Where do we fill in fallback paths for the local model weights and its executable, plus a shorter waiting limit, but only when the surrounding process has not already set them itself?
queries.why: Uses setdefault / not-set guards so an externally configured runtime is never overwritten.

queries.question: How does dropping a new folder containing a manifest into a known directory make a fresh capability available, and what happens when that manifest fails its checks?
queries.why: Iterates skills_lib subfolders, loads each skill.json, drops invalid ones into an error list and dynamically imports handlers.

queries.question: Where are accented Polish letters folded onto their plain equivalents and plural endings chopped off, so that a lookup word and an indexed word collapse into the same form?
queries.why: Lowercases, applies an explicit diacritics translation table, then EN and PL suffix stripping; used identically for queries and indexed text.

queries.question: Which code sends a chat request over a REST call to the resident local language-model service and converts every possible failure — refused connection, exceeded deadline, malformed body, empty answer — into a plain result dictionary instead of raising?
queries.why: POSTs to /v1/chat/completions and wraps everything in try/except returning {'ok': False, ...}; never propagates an exception.

queries.question: Where is a refused connection or an expired deadline while talking to the local model daemon turned into a readable message telling the user to start that daemon or raise the waiting limit?
queries.why: Catches ConnectError and TimeoutException and re-raises LLMError with an actionable Polish hint; also computes tokens per second.

queries.question: Where does a worker machine keep reporting that it is alive at a fixed cadence, carrying on after a failed network round-trip, and never letting the pause between reports fall below five seconds?
queries.why: Endless tick cycle that catches HTTPError/URLError, prints to stderr and sleeps max(5, interval).
queries.leak_check: symbol tokens 'run','loop' absent from question; module-name tokens 'node','heartbeat' also avoided

queries.question: Where is a newly rebuilt catalogue of everything on disk written under a temporary name first and only then swapped into place, so a crash cannot leave a half-written listing behind?
queries.why: Writes to a .tmp sibling then calls os.replace for an atomic swap.

queries.question: What gives an exact filename match a much higher standing than a mere fragment found somewhere deep in the full path, when ordering local lookup results?
queries.why: Tiered integer weights 150/120/90/70/55/40 depending on where and how the term matches.

queries.question: Where do we pull readable prose out of a downloaded HTML page, discarding scripts, styling and navigation chrome, and inserting line breaks at block-level markup?
queries.why: HTMLParser subclass that ignores script/style/noscript/nav/footer/header and appends newlines for p/br/div/li/section/article/h1-h3.

queries.question: What prevents the crawler from downloading a page whose host lies outside a fixed allow-list of reputable sites?
queries.why: Parses the netloc and requires it to end with one of the allow-listed hosts; anything else is skipped before fetching.

queries.question: Where do we merge time-limited obligations coming from two separate lists in the stored personal work profile, drop repeats, keep only what falls inside a two-week horizon plus anything already past its date, and order the most pressing first?
queries.why: Merges the explicit list with per-case dates, dedupes by id, filters against a horizon and returns overdue plus in-window sorted by days left.

queries.question: Where is the whole command-line flag surface of the record-lifecycle tool declared — admitting a new item, noting that somebody opened one, passing sentence, and the preview-versus-actually-move switch?
queries.why: Single place defining --admit, --record-drill, --record-outline, --judge, --apply, --status and the threshold flags.

queries.question: Where is a role definition rejected outright when any mandatory attribute is missing, empty or of the wrong shape, instead of quietly receiving a fallback value?
queries.why: Fail-closed checker over REQUIRED_FIELDS plus id prefix, allowed-pattern list, ceiling vocabulary and tier vocabulary; returns a list of errors that makes the caller drop the definition.

queries.question: Where do we read a capability manifest off disk and still accept an older field name that used to carry the object's category?
queries.why: Builds AObject from JSON and falls back to the legacy 'kind' key when 'type' is absent.

queries.question: When the shared vector service cannot be reached and we silently drop down to the local embedded database instead, where is that downgrade made visible by appending a timestamped line into a dedicated runtime file?
queries.why: Emits an error through the standard logger and appends 'DEGRADED_TO_EMBEDDED reason=...' to aions_store_degraded.log because stdout is not captured.

queries.question: How is the raw closeness number returned by the vector index converted into a normalised zero-through-one relevance value, accounting for which geometry the collection was actually built under?
queries.why: Branches on hnsw:space — cosine/ip use 1-d, unset/l2 is squared L2 so it uses 1-(d/2) — then clamps into 0..1.

queries.question: Where do we compute one weighted number for choosing between two competing capabilities, trading off how often each one succeeds against how quickly it finishes, under three selectable preference modes?
queries.why: Blends success ratio and a speed term with weights that differ for 'fast', 'reliable' and the balanced default.

queries.question: Where do we decide that the current number of system error entries is genuinely abnormal by comparing it against the rolling mean of the previous few rounds, and why does the very first round never raise an alarm?
queries.why: Pure read that requires both an absolute threshold and more than twice the mean of the last five samples; an empty history only seeds the mean.

queries.question: Where do we refuse a further attempt at bouncing the same service once it has already been bounced three times inside a half-hour sliding window?
queries.why: Prunes timestamps older than the window and allows the action only while fewer than three remain.

queries.question: Where do we guarantee that a diagnostic answer comes back inside a fixed number of seconds even when the underlying work hangs during slow initialisation, by pushing it onto a throwaway background thread and waiting on a single-slot queue?
queries.why: Daemon thread puts its outcome into a one-element queue; queue.Empty after the deadline yields an error marker instead of blocking.

queries.question: When a reply would be too large for the model's context window, where is the whole body parked in memory behind a short reference identifier and only a size summary handed back instead?
queries.why: Beyond an 800-character threshold it stores the serialized payload under an OFF_ id and returns the id plus a per-key size digest.

queries.question: Where is an already-computed retrieval outcome stashed on disk under a digest of the question, and what stops that file from growing without bound?
queries.why: Writes {ts, query, top_k, result} under a sha1-derived key and trims to the 500 newest entries when it overflows.

queries.question: Why is the connection object for the embedding database created just once per process and then reused, and what slow behaviour did that change fix?
queries.why: In-process singleton; the comment records that recreating it per retrieval caused a full collection re-initialisation of roughly 18 seconds.

queries.question: How do we pull the JSON object out of an event-stream reply whose body is a series of lines carrying a field label prefix, while still coping with a body that is just plain JSON?
queries.why: Scans lines for the 'data:' prefix and decodes the remainder; otherwise decodes the entire body.

queries.question: Where do we walk a module's abstract syntax tree in order to list what it depends on, and which regular-expression fallback takes over when that tree cannot be built because the source is malformed?
queries.why: ast.walk over Import/ImportFrom nodes, with a regex over '^(from|import) name' after SyntaxError.

queries.question: Where are tens of thousands of discovered paths chewed through by a pool of eight worker threads, with each finished result folded into shared totals behind a mutex and progress printed every five hundred items?
queries.why: ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) plus as_completed, updating self.result under threading.Lock.

queries.question: Which end-to-end check hits the external appointment service using a real stored grant, prints today's and tomorrow's entries plus the next ten upcoming ones, and confirms the grant can still be renewed without ever printing the credential itself?
queries.why: Checks the client and token files exist, lists ranges, then calls the renewal verification and strips the token file path out of the printed status.
queries.leak_check: symbol token 'main' absent from question; module tokens 'calendar','smoke' also avoided

queries.question: Before anything encrypted is unlocked, where do we confirm that a small sentinel blob still decrypts correctly for the current Windows account, and refuse the whole operation otherwise?
queries.why: Reads .aions_operator.key, unprotects it through DPAPI with the fixed entropy and raises unless the plaintext matches the expected constant.

queries.question: Where is machine-written handler code byte-compiled and then imported inside a throwaway subprocess, checked for a callable entry point, and only after that copied into the live library?
queries.why: Runs py_compile then an importlib exec_module probe printing OK/NORUN, moving the request to failed on either failure before copytree into skills_lib.

queries.question: How do we roll back a failed database schema migration and return the store to the previous revision?
queries.why: No migration framework or versioned schema exists anywhere in scope; a case-insensitive search for alembic/migration/migrate/schema_version/downgrade over aions_core, server, mcpServers, control_plane, tools and scripts returned only prose inside memory chunk data files, zero code.

queries.question: Where do we throttle how many requests a single caller may send per minute and answer with a too-many-requests status once that budget is spent?
queries.why: No throttling anywhere; grepping ratelimit/rate_limit/throttl/429 over all in-scope directories hit only stored knowledge chunks and index blobs, never source. The FastAPI apps (server/app.py, control_plane/api.py) register no such middleware or dependency.

queries.question: Which endpoint exposes counters and histograms for a monitoring system to scrape, and how are those measurements registered?
queries.why: No instrumentation library is used; prometheus/opentelemetry/otel/statsd/metrics_exporter match nothing in source. The only health surfaces are plain JSON dictionaries (/health, /status, system_health) with no measurement registry behind them.

queries.question: How does the system send a message to somebody's inbox when a serious problem is detected?
queries.why: There is no outbound mail path at all: smtp/smtplib/sendmail/sendgrid/mailgun match nothing, and the single 'mailto' occurrence is a URL-scheme filter inside scripts/project_scanner.py. Escalations go to JSONL incident files and stderr only.

queries.question: Where are user-facing strings kept in per-language catalogues so the interface can be shown in a different tongue?
queries.why: No localisation machinery: gettext/i18n/babel/.po/translation catalogues match nothing in source; the sole 'locale' hit is a profile field printed verbatim in scripts/ingest_tier1_chroma.py. Polish and English strings are hardcoded inline.

queries.question: How do we switch a new behaviour on for only a slice of traffic and turn it back off without redeploying?
queries.why: No gradual-rollout mechanism exists; feature_flag/launchdarkly/unleash/rollout match only memory chunk data, never code. Behaviour is toggled solely by all-or-nothing environment variables read at import time.
